preview.headline: Hurricanes Host Struggling Kraken in Quick Rematch
preview.summary: Just two days after a 4-1 victory in Seattle, the surging Carolina Hurricanes welcome the Seattle Kraken for a quick-turnaround rematch. Both teams enter with identical rest of one full calendar day, but they sit on opposite ends of the league's performance spectrum.
preview.away_analysis: The Kraken are mired in a two-game losing streak and facing deep structural challenges across the board. Ranking 32nd in Corsi For percentage at 42.08 and 31st in expected goals percentage, Seattle struggles badly to control possession and generate offense at 5-on-5. A brutal 65.22 percent penalty kill ranking 30th compounds their defensive issues, leaving them heavily reliant on occasional power play success to stay competitive.
preview.home_analysis: The Hurricanes are firing on all cylinders, riding a three-game winning streak while dominating the underlying metrics. Carolina paces the entire NHL in Corsi For percentage, expected goals percentage, and high-danger chance share, overwhelming opponents with a relentless 66.27 shot attempts per 60 minutes. Backed by Kochetkov's top-tier goaltending, the Hurricanes control play from start to finish.
matchup_edges: Carolina owns a massive territorial advantage, ranking 1st in Corsi For % and expected goals share compared to Seattle's 32nd-ranked possession profile.
The Hurricanes feature an elite penalty kill sitting 8th in the league, a severe mismatch against a Kraken side struggling with a 30th-ranked penalty kill.
Carolina's high-danger chance generation ranks 1st overall, putting immense pressure on a Seattle defense that bleeds chances.
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution, particularly whether Seattle can avoid handing Carolina's capable power play extra opportunities while fixing their own defensive zone coverage.
preview.key_question: Can the Kraken find an answer for Carolina's suffocating forecheck after managing just one goal in their previous meeting?
preview.quick_takeaway: The Hurricanes hold a commanding advantage in every major statistical category over a struggling Kraken squad.

preview.headline: Hot Jets Visit United Center to Take on Struggling Blackhawks
preview.summary: The Winnipeg Jets bring a five-game winning streak into Chicago to face a Blackhawks team looking to build on a single win. Winnipeg holds the overall statistical advantage across almost every metrics category, while Chicago struggles to generate offense and control play.
preview.away_analysis: The Jets are riding high on a five-game winning streak, though their underlying numbers suggest they are playing a tighter brand of hockey than their record implies. Ranking 23rd in Corsi For% (48.84%) and 19th in expected goals share, Winnipeg relies on a strong power play ranking 10th in the league at 24.19% to help tilt results in their favor. However, they take penalties at a high rate, ranking 8th in penalties taken per 60.
preview.home_analysis: The Blackhawks have faced a difficult uphill battle this season, sitting near the bottom of the league in nearly all possession and scoring metrics. Ranking 30th in Corsi For% and 32nd in Goals For%, Chicago struggles immensely to generate sustained offense, posting a league-worst 11.11% power play. Knight will need a massive performance in net to counter Winnipeg's special teams advantage.
matchup_edges: Winnipeg holds a massive special teams advantage with a top-10 power play facing Chicago's league-worst 31st-ranked unit efficiency.
The Jets enter with elite momentum, riding a five-game win streak compared to Chicago's 32nd-ranked goal-scoring percentage.
Winnipeg controls possession much more effectively, ranking well ahead of Chicago's 30th-ranked Corsi For%.
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution, particularly whether Chicago can stay out of the penalty box against Winnipeg's potent power play.
preview.key_question: Can the Blackhawks find a way to generate high-danger chances against a structured Jets team, or will Winnipeg's special teams dictate the pace?
preview.quick_takeaway: The red-hot Jets look to exploit Chicago's league-worst offense and stagnant power play to extend their winning streak on the road.

preview.headline: Panthers and Blues Meet in St. Louis Riding Matching Two-Game Win Streaks
preview.summary: Both the Florida Panthers and St. Louis Blues enter tonight's matchup on a two-game winning streak despite underlying scoring struggles that have kept their actual goal shares lower than expected. Both teams boast elite penalty kills sitting inside the top five, pointing toward a tightly contested battle where special teams efficiency will be heavily tested.
preview.away_analysis: The Panthers control the puck exceptionally well, ranking 5th in Corsi For percentage and 3rd in Corsi Against per 60, but they struggle to finish with a bottom-tier 8.76 shooting percentage dragging down their actual goals share. Their strong defensive suppression keeps expected goals against at an elite level, and they pair it with a stellar penalty kill ranked 4th in the league. However, their discipline remains a glaring weakness as they take penalties at the highest rate in the NHL.
preview.home_analysis: The Blues generate high-danger looks efficiently, ranking 10th in high-danger chance percentage and 8th in expected goals for per 60, yet a woeful 7.19 shooting percentage has suppressed their actual goal output. They struggle to suppress shot attempts against, ranking 29th in Corsi Against per 60, but compensate with immense discipline by taking the second-fewest penalties in the league. Goalie Hofer has been a standout presence recently, anchoring the defensive unit with a top-five GSAx ranking over his last 20 games.
matchup_edges: Florida holds a major territorial advantage in shot-attempt suppression, ranking 3rd in Corsi Against per 60 compared to St. Louis at 29th.
St. Louis boasts a notable edge in recent goaltending form with Hofer ranking 4th in GSAx over his last 20 games, well ahead of Markstrom at 22nd.
The Blues maintain a huge discipline advantage, taking the 2nd-fewest penalties per 60 while the Panthers take the absolute most in the league.
preview.x_factor: Panthers penalty kill versus Blues discipline, as Florida's elite 4th-ranked PK faces a St. Louis squad that rarely hands out power-play opportunities.
preview.key_question: Can either team break out of their offensive slump and finally align their strong expected-goal metrics with actual scoring conversion?
preview.quick_takeaway: Florida dominates possession and shot suppression, but St. Louis counters with superior discipline and high-end recent goaltending from Hofer.

preview.headline: Devils and Capitals Meet for Immediate Rematch in Washington
preview.summary: Following a decisive 5-2 victory just two days ago, the New Jersey Devils travel to face the Washington Capitals again in an immediate back-to-back head-to-head set.
preview.away_analysis: The Devils bring an elite analytical profile into this matchup, ranking 3rd in Corsi For% (53.82%) and 4th in Expected Goals% (55.36%). They suppress shots and chances brilliantly, ranking 3rd in expected goals against per 60, though their special teams feature a glaring vulnerability with a 31st-ranked penalty kill (65.12%).
preview.home_analysis: The Capitals sit in the middle of the pack analytically, posting a 49.96% expected goals share that ranks 17th in the league. While they draw plenty of penalties, their discipline issues result in taking 4.21 minors per 60, and they will need a much stronger defensive effort than they showed in Wednesday's loss.
matchup_edges: New Jersey controls play significantly better at 5-on-5, holding strong advantages in both Corsi For% and Expected Goals%.
The Devils suppress scoring chances at an elite level, ranking 3rd in expected goals against per 60 compared to Washington's 16th-ranked defense.
Washington takes considerably more penalties than New Jersey, creating a major discipline disparity.
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution, particularly whether Washington can exploit New Jersey's league-worst 31st-ranked penalty kill.
preview.key_question: Can the Capitals make the necessary adjustments after a lopsided loss to the Devils just two nights ago?
preview.quick_takeaway: The Devils own a clear territorial and defensive advantage at 5-on-5, but their struggles on the penalty kill give the Capitals a clear avenue to bounce back.

preview.headline: Wild Visit Bruins in Interconference Clash of Playoff Contenders
preview.summary: The Minnesota Wild hit the road to face the Boston Bruins, looking to build on a two-game winning streak. Both teams met earlier this season on October 3, where the Wild secured a 4-1 victory at home.
preview.away_analysis: The Wild arrive with strong underlying metrics, ranking 5th in expected goals percentage at 54.95% and 2nd in goals for percentage. Paced by an elite offense that generates 2.97 expected goals per 60 minutes and goalie Wallstedt anchoring the net with the league's top GSAx rank over his last 20 games, Minnesota controls play effectively at both ends.
preview.home_analysis: The Bruins lean on strong finishing prowess, ranking 4th in shooting percentage at 11.81% to mask mediocre possession metrics like a 21st-ranked Corsi For percentage. Boston struggles to stay out of the penalty box, taking 4.78 penalties per 60 minutes which ranks 29th in the league, while their power play sits down at 27th overall.
matchup_edges: Minnesota holds a clear edge in territorial control and high-danger chance generation, ranking 5th in HDCF% compared to Boston at 9th.
The Wild possess a significant special teams advantage, particularly on the power play where they rank 6th against Boston's 27th-ranked unit.
Minnesota features elite goaltending form with Wallstedt holding the top GSAx rank over his last 20 games, giving them stability against Boston's lethal shooting talent.
preview.x_factor: Boston's discipline and penalty trouble; taking 4.78 penalties per 60 minutes against Minnesota's potent 6th-ranked power play could prove fatal.
preview.key_question: Can the Bruins' high shooting percentage continue to overcome their possession deficits against Wallstedt and an airtight Wild defense?
preview.quick_takeaway: Minnesota's superior possession and special teams metrics give them the upper hand, but Boston's high-end finishing ability keeps them dangerous.

preview.headline: Oilers Visit Maple Leafs As Edmonton Rides Three-Game Win Streak
preview.summary: The Edmonton Oilers travel to face the Toronto Maple Leafs on November 14, 2026, looking to extend a three-game winning streak against a Toronto squad mired in a five-game slide. Toronto previously dominated the first meeting with a 7-2 victory on October 24, but both teams enter this matchup looking to assert control over middling underlying possession numbers.
preview.away_analysis: The Oilers bring a three-game win streak and two days of rest into this matchup, though their underlying metrics suggest they have survived rather than dominated. Edmonton ranks 26th in expected goals percentage (44.75%) and 27th in Corsi For percentage, struggling to generate sustained pressure at 5-v-5. However, their elite power play ranks 3rd in the league and serves as a major equalizer, capable of masking their bottom-tier shot-attempt suppression and chance generation.
preview.home_analysis: The Maple Leafs are desperate to snap a five-game losing streak despite playing their fourth game in seven days with just one day of rest. Toronto holds slight territorial advantages over Edmonton, ranking 18th in expected goals percentage and boasting a better high-danger chance share. Furthermore, their special teams remain formidable with a top-10 penalty kill and a dangerous power play ranking 7th.
matchup_edges: Edmonton's 3rd-ranked power play holds a clear advantage over Toronto's penalty kill in special teams efficiency.
Toronto claims the better territorial play, ranking higher in expected goals percentage and high-danger chance share.
The Oilers enjoy a rest advantage with two full days off compared to Toronto's congested recent schedule.
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution will likely decide the game, as Edmonton's lethal power play tests Toronto's disciplined penalty-killing unit.
preview.key_question: Can the Maple Leafs snap their five-game losing streak despite playing a heavy schedule, or will the rested Oilers capitalize on special teams?
preview.quick_takeaway: Edmonton brings rest and a top-tier power play into Toronto, while the struggling Maple Leafs look to replicate their dominant 7-2 head-to-head win from October.

preview.headline: Avalanche Visit Canadiens in Clash of Contrasting Shot Metrics and Finishing
preview.summary: The Colorado Avalanche travel to face the Montreal Canadiens in a matchup featuring heavy volume versus elite finishing, with both teams navigating a busy early-season schedule.
preview.away_analysis: The Avalanche drive play exceptionally well at 5-on-5, ranking 7th in Corsi For % and 2nd in shot attempts generated per 60. However, their underlying expected goals percentage sits down at 24th due to a 27th-ranked high-danger chance share, meaning their heavy volume often comes from the perimeter. Special teams provide stability with top-tier efficiency, though Blackwood holds a modest 28th-ranked GSAx over his last 20 games.
preview.home_analysis: The Canadiens boast an elite 3rd-ranked goals-for percentage driven by an exceptional 2nd-ranked shooting percentage, significantly outperforming their underlying expected metrics. Montreal struggles to suppress chances, ranking 30th in expected goals against per 60 and taking penalties at one of the highest rates in the league. Fortunately, Fowler has been exceptional, anchoring the defense with the 2nd-best GSAx ranking over his last 20 appearances.
matchup_edges: Colorado holds a massive territorial advantage in shot-attempt generation at 5-on-5.
Montreal boasts a significant finishing edge, backed by a top-2 shooting percentage.
The Canadiens hold a major edge in recent goaltending performance via Fowler's elite GSAx ranking.
preview.x_factor: Canadiens goaltender Fowler holding firm against Colorado's high-volume shot generation.
preview.key_question: Can Montreal continue to overperform its expected goals metrics with elite shooting, or will Colorado's territorial control wear them down?
preview.quick_takeaway: Colorado brings heavy shot volume and strong possession, but Montreal counters with elite finishing efficiency and stellar recent goaltending from Fowler.

preview.headline: Red Wings Look to Snap Skid Against High-Flying Lightning
preview.summary: The Detroit Red Wings travel to face the Tampa Bay Lightning on November 14, 2026, desperately seeking to reverse a five-game losing streak. Meanwhile, the Lightning enter this matchup riding a two-game win streak and holding a decisive early-season edge in overall possession and finishing talent.
preview.away_analysis: Detroit is mired in a five-game slide despite generating solid high-danger looks, ranking 7th in high-danger chances percentage (53.68%). However, their finishing has lagged behind their underlying expected goals percentage (51.13%), dragged down by a lowly 8.53% shooting percentage. Special teams remain a glaring vulnerability, particularly a penalty kill that sits 27th in the league at 70.49%.
preview.home_analysis: Tampa Bay controls play effectively, ranking 2nd in both Corsi For% (53.92%) and high-danger chances percentage (56.9%). Their elite 14.0% shooting percentage powers a potent offense that ranks 4th in goals for percentage (63.64%). Like Detroit, their penalty kill struggles at 71.7%, but their dominant five-on-five shot control keeps pressure off their goaltending.
matchup_edges: Tampa Bay holds a massive advantage in five-on-five shot and chance suppression, ranking 2nd in Corsi For% compared to Detroit's 14th.
The Lightning boast the league's top shooting percentage (14.0%), heavily outmatching a Red Wings squad struggling to finish at 23rd.
Detroit maintains a respectable high-danger chance share (7th), presenting a pathway to test Tampa Bay if they can capitalize on opportunities.
preview.x_factor: Lightning goaltender Vasilevskiy ranks 34th in GSAx over his last 20 games, giving a struggling Detroit offense an opening to find its rhythm.
preview.key_question: Can the Red Wings leverage their strong high-danger chance generation to crack a rolling Tampa Bay squad?
preview.quick_takeaway: Tampa Bay's dominant possession metrics and lethal shooting talent clash with a desperate Detroit side desperately needing special teams improvement.

preview.headline: Underlying Powerhouses Clash as Penguins Host Senators
preview.summary: An intriguing matchup features two teams controlling possession and generating strong underlying metrics, though the Penguins are severely underperforming their expected goals while the Senators are converting efficiently.
preview.away_analysis: The Senators bring strong possession metrics into this matchup, ranking eighth in Corsi For percentage at 52.85 percent and expected goals percentage at 53.59 percent. They supplement this play with a top-tier shooting percentage of 10.98 percent that ranks seventh overall, helping drive their strong actual goals percentage. However, special teams remain a glaring weakness, with a power play sitting 31st in the league at 11.84 percent.
preview.home_analysis: The Penguins are a statistical anomaly, dominating play with a 54.91 expected goals percentage that ranks sixth and a high-danger chance share of 55.91 percent that ranks third. Despite generating plenty of chances with an expected goals for mark of 2.92 per 60, their actual goal results are dragged down by a paltry 7.81 shooting percentage that ranks 27th. Discipline is a major asset for Pittsburgh, taking just 3.09 penalties per 60 to rank third best in the league.
matchup_edges: Penguins hold a massive high-danger chance share advantage, ranking 3rd in HDCF% compared to the Senators at 19th.
Senators boast a superior finishing touch, sitting 7th in shooting percentage while the Penguins languish at 27th.
Penguins excel at discipline, taking the 3rd fewest penalties per 60 minutes in the NHL.
preview.x_factor: Puck luck and finishing efficiency, as Pittsburgh dominates chance generation but cannot buy a goal.
preview.key_question: Will the Penguins finally break their shooting slump against a Senators squad that keeps shot attempts relatively suppressed?
preview.quick_takeaway: Pittsburgh dominates the underlying chance battle, but Ottawa's superior finishing efficiency makes this an unpredictable duel of contrasting realities.

preview.headline: Flyers Visit Blue Jackets Looking to Capitalize on Underlying Metrics
preview.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers travel to take on the Columbus Blue Jackets in a matchup featuring two teams struggling with finishing efficiency, though the Flyers hold a significant edge in underlying possession and defensive suppression.
preview.away_analysis: The Flyers control play reasonably well with a 50.17 Corsi For % and boast a strong expected goals share at 53.56%, ranking 9th in the league. Their defense is exceptionally stingy, allowing just 2.31 expected goals against per 60 to rank 4th. However, a low 8.43% shooting percentage has dragged actual results down, keeping their goal differential closer to earth.
preview.home_analysis: The Blue Jackets enter on a three-game losing streak while battling severe offensive and defensive struggles across the board. Columbus ranks near the bottom in expected goals percentage at 44.5% and holds a league-worst 5.74% shooting percentage. Their penalty kill also lags at 73.91%, compounding defensive suppression issues that see them allow nearly three expected goals against per 60.
matchup_edges: Philadelphia holds a massive advantage in expected goals suppression, ranking 4th compared to Columbus at 28th.
The Flyers generate a superior quality of chances, sitting 9th in expected goals percentage while the Blue Jackets sit down in 27th.
Columbus struggles significantly on special teams with a 23rd-ranked penalty kill against a Philadelphia side looking to find traction on the power play.
preview.x_factor: Columbus goaltender Greaves, who carries a heavy workload behind a struggling defense that surrenders high-danger opportunities at an alarming rate.
preview.key_question: Can the Blue Jackets find any finish to support a defense that routinely gets caved in on expected goals?
preview.quick_takeaway: Philadelphia controls the underlying metrics across the board, but they will need to break through their finishing slump to convert territorial advantage into an actual win.

preview.headline: Stars Host Sabres Looking to Bounce Back on Home Ice
preview.summary: The Buffalo Sabres visit the Dallas Stars on November 14, 2026, looking to snap a three-game losing streak while dealing with a busier recent schedule. Dallas took the first meeting of the season 4-0 on October 8 and enters with a rested advantage in special teams and defensive suppression.
preview.away_analysis: The Sabres control play well at 5-on-5, ranking 6th in Corsi For % and boasting an elite 2nd-ranked expected goals for rate at 2.99 per 60. However, a 3-game losing streak and a congested schedule with 3 games in the last 7 days highlight their current hurdles. Their underlying metrics are undercut by bottom-tier special teams, ranking 29th on the power play and 28th on the penalty kill.
preview.home_analysis: The Stars boast a stifling defense, giving up the fewest expected goals per 60 in the league and ranking 2nd in Corsi Against per 60. Their expected goals percentage sits 3rd overall at 56.33%, though their actual goal share lags behind at 44.0%. Dallas features a potent top-10 power play and an elite 3rd-ranked penalty kill that will pose a major challenge to Buffalo's struggling units.
matchup_edges: Dallas owns a massive special teams advantage, anchored by the league's 3rd-ranked penalty kill against Buffalo's 28th-ranked unit.
The Stars suppress chances at an elite level, ranking 1st in expected goals against per 60.
Buffalo generates high-volume offense, sitting 2nd in expected goals for per 60 compared to Dallas at 18th.
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution, where Dallas holds a decisive edge on both the power play and penalty kill.
preview.key_question: Can Buffalo's high-generating offense finally break through Dallas's top-ranked defensive suppression?
preview.quick_takeaway: Dallas holds a commanding edge in defensive suppression and special teams, though Buffalo's strong shot-generation metrics keep them dangerous if they can solve the Stars' stifling structure.

preview.headline: Mammoth Seek Breakthrough Against Sharks Amid Underlying Dominance
preview.summary: The Utah Mammoth host the San Jose Sharks looking to snap a four-game skid despite strong underlying metrics, while the Sharks arrive searching for defensive stability after struggling heavily in expected goals and high-danger chance share.
preview.away_analysis: The Sharks rank near the bottom of the league in expected goals percentage (30th) and high-danger chance share (30th), getting routinely out-chanced at 5-on-5. Their defensive suppression is a major concern, surrendering 3.35 expected goals against per 60 minutes, which ranks last in the NHL. However, Askarov provides a stabilizing presence in net with an 11th-ranked GSAx over his last 20 games.
preview.home_analysis: The Mammoth control play brilliantly, ranking 2nd in expected goals percentage and 4th in high-danger chance share, but they are sinking under a brutal 40.38% actual goals share and a four-game losing streak. Their elite chance generation is severely undermined by a 7.45% shooting percentage and a struggling penalty kill ranking 26th in the league. Vejmelka has also struggled to find traction, sitting 66th in GSAx over his last 20 appearances.
matchup_edges: Utah holds a massive territorial advantage, ranking 2nd in expected goals for per 60 against San Jose's 32nd-ranked expected goals against suppression.
The Mammoth possess a lethal power play clicking at 34.33% (2nd) that could exploit San Jose's 20th-ranked penalty kill.
San Jose holds a clear edge in goaltending form based on Askarov's strong recent GSAx ranking compared to Vejmelka.
preview.x_factor: Special teams efficiency, where Utah's elite power play matches up against San Jose's penalty kill and penalty-taking frequency.
preview.key_question: Can the Mammoth finally translate their elite territorial dominance and chance generation into actual goals, or will their finishing woes persist?
preview.quick_takeaway: Utah dominates the underlying metrics and chance creation but needs finishing and saves to turn territorial control into actual wins against a struggling San Jose squad.

preview.headline: Islanders Head West to Face Ducks in Interconference Matchup
preview.summary: The New York Islanders travel to Anaheim to take on the Ducks on November 14, 2026, looking to build on a recent win while the Ducks seek to bounce back from a loss. Both squads sit outside the league's top tier in play-play metrics, but contrasting special teams and goaltending landscapes create an intriguing tactical battle.
preview.away_analysis: The Islanders bring a strong penalty kill that ranks 6th in the league at 85.71% and a disciplined approach that keeps them out of the penalty box, ranking 27th in penalties taken per 60. While their overall expected goals percentage sits 22nd at 48.69%, their expected goals for per 60 ranks a respectable 10th. With Sorokin anchoring the crease with a strong 6th-ranked GSAx over his last 20 games, New York has reliable backend support to weather defensive zone pressure.
preview.home_analysis: The Ducks lean heavily on an elite power play that clicks at 36.76% to lead the entire NHL. However, Anaheim struggles significantly with shot-share and chance generation, ranking 28th in expected goals percentage and 31st in high-danger chances share at 40.4%. Their defensive suppression also lags, yielding a 31st-ranked expected goals against per 60 while Dostal holds a 48th-ranked GSAx over his last 20 appearances.
matchup_edges: Anaheim power play (1st) facing the Islanders penalty kill (6th)
New York goaltending advantage with Sorokin's strong recent GSAx rank of 6
Islanders advantage in expected goals for per 60 (10th vs Ducks' 23rd)
preview.x_factor: Anaheim's top-ranked power play must find a way to break through a disciplined New York penalty kill that stays out of the box and limits high-danger opportunities.
preview.key_question: Can the Ducks generate enough sustained 5-on-5 offense to overcome their defensive struggles against a superior Islanders goaltender?
preview.quick_takeaway: An elite Anaheim power play squares off against a disciplined Islanders side relying on Sorokin's stellar recent form and a shutdown penalty kill.
